title: God's divine council in Genesis: 'Behold, man has become like us'

tellings.quote: he turns to this divine council, this mysterious council full of other beings in heaven. That's way very much often overlooked. And he says, "Behold, man has become like us."

plain: A researcher named Luke Caverns says that in the Garden of Eden story in Genesis, God turns to a "divine council", a group of other beings in heaven, and says "Behold, man has become like us", a detail he thinks people usually overlook. In the King James Bible of 1611, which he credits, the verse reads "Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil." The plural "us" is in the text, so the verse does have God speaking to or for more than himself; who that "us" is, a council of beings or something else, the verse does not say.
